domain.text: developer tooling: TypeScript npm package skeleton and CLI (vworlds/vmethod PR 14, issue 3)

impressions.text: The domain is developer tooling — a strict-TypeScript npm package skeleton for the vmethod CLI with validated YAML config, offline check/init verbs and OIDC publishing — delivered as PR 14 against issue 3.
The worker delivered the requested scope end-to-end and re-ran full local validation (format:check, lint, typecheck, test, build, smoke, knip) after every round, with CI green on each push.

Review twice caught that models.tsv handling did not match the real vecs and SpaceRocks files — first the commented header and provider/id column, then gate '-' versus 'none' and unprefixed claude-kind model ids — where the worker's synthetic fixture had passed.

Other review catches were a versioning defect (stale changelog fragments would keep bumping the major/minor at every release) and a security-relevant env mapping that could have let VMETHOD_OWNER name the owner, fixed by dropping the switch so authority comes only from people.yaml.

Stops and escalations were explicit: the worker never attempted real npm publication pending the owner's trusted-publisher setup, and the approve-and-merge decision was escalated to the owner, who had already set the MIT-license and vecs-style release decisions on issue 3.
The PR merged on 2026-10-16 after three review rounds, with points unchanged at 8 open and 8 final.

roundCauses.text: Round 2 was caused by review round 1 requesting changes for four defects: stale changelog fragments counted at every release, models.tsv conversion failing on the real files, wrong VMETHOD_OWNER/VMETHOD_BOARD_PROJECT mappings, and stub root lookup failing when git is installed but no repository exists.

Round 3 was caused by review round 2 finding the TSV fix still failing on the real files because ungated rows use gate '-' rather than 'none' and kind 'claude' rows carry bare model ids without a provider prefix, with the worker told to ship verbatim copies of the real files as fixtures.

findings.text: Old changelog fragments in changes/unreleased/ were consumed at every release, so one landed 'breaking' fragment would bump the major version and every 'feature' would bump the minor on all later releases; releasePlan now counts only fragments added since the previous release tag.

models.tsv conversion failed on the real vecs and SpaceRocks dev files: the header is a comment line, the column is provider/id rather than model, ungated rows use gate '-', and kind 'claude' rows have no provider prefix.

VMETHOD_OWNER and VMETHOD_BOARD_PROJECT were mapped to the wrong things; both switches were dropped because an environment variable must never be able to grant owner authority, which comes only from people.yaml.

A stub failed when git was installed but there was no repository, because git rev-parse ran before VMETHOD_ROOT was considered; the fix prefers VMETHOD_ROOT, then git discovery, then the failure message.
